successCriteria.description: scripts/smoke.js retains stages 1–3d (migrate, boot, probe incl. 3a mount / 3b auth-enforced / 3c token-populates-user / 3d persistence) unchanged in behavior — the edit only EXTENDS after 3d and never weakens or deletes an existing assertion.

The Postgres seed block mints the seeded employee's password_hash via bcrypt.hashSync(SMOKE_PASSWORD, 10) where SMOKE_PASSWORD comes from process.env (defaulting to a non-secret placeholder) — no credential string is hardcoded in the file.

The seed block adds a second leave type (SICK) with an effective ACTIVE policy (pol-2) but NO leave_balances row, alongside the existing ANNUAL type/policy/balance — the fixture that proves getCurrentBalances omits an effective policy lacking a balance row.

A login stage POSTs the seeded employee's email + SMOKE_PASSWORD and asserts a 200 with a non-empty token string and a profile whose id and email match the seeded employee (real values, not just status).

A profile stage uses the login token to GET /employees/me and asserts the exact 10-field EmployeeProfile (id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, role, managerId, department, hireDate, employmentStatus) with passwordHash and terminationDate absent.
A list stage uses the login token to GET /leaves and asserts the request created in stage 3d is present in the returned array (EMPLOYEE role scoping to the owner).

A getById stage uses the login token to GET /leaves/:id with the id captured from the stage 3d POST response body (not predicted) and asserts the seeded request is returned with matching id and employeeId.

A balances stage re-keys the seeded balance to the CURRENT accrual period via periodContaining(hireDate, 12, new Date()) imported from src/shared/date, then GET /balances/me and asserts EXACTLY one balance (ANNUAL) with correct periodStart/periodEnd and available === 25 — the SICK type (effective policy, no balance row) is omitted.

constraints: The new stages (login/profile/list/getById/balances) run ONLY in Postgres mode (SMOKE_DATABASE_URL set); in sqlite mode they are skipped with the existing persistence caveat and must not fail the run.
No credential string is hardcoded in scripts/smoke.js — the seeded password plaintext comes from process.env.SMOKE_PASSWORD (no-hardcoded-secrets).

Stages 1–3d (migrate, boot, 3a mount, 3b auth-enforced, 3c token-populates-user, 3d persistence) are preserved verbatim — the edit only appends after 3d and never weakens or deletes an existing assertion.

Stages 5–8 must authenticate with the token returned by POST /auth/login (a genuine login token minted under the same JWT_SECRET registerAuth verifies), not the hand-minted signToken used by stages 3b/3c.
outOfScope: Unit/integration tests (tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts, tests/unit/modules/auth/auth.service.test.ts) — owned by Sub-phase 7.3; do not create or require them here.

Sub-phase 7.1 deliverables (src/modules/employee/employee.routes.ts, src/modules/employee/index.ts, src/app.ts) — produced by a sibling; this phase must not create them and must not be gated on their presence.
No production source changes — the only project file touched is scripts/smoke.js.

entityInvariants.invariant: The seeded employee's passwordHash is a bcrypt hash of SMOKE_PASSWORD (cost 10); it is never returned in any response (profile omits passwordHash).
Exactly one balance row exists for the seeded employee (ANNUAL); the SICK leave type has an effective ACTIVE policy but no balance row, so getCurrentBalances omits it rather than synthesizing.
The request created in stage 3d is owned by the seeded employee (employeeId = EMP) and is visible to that employee via list and getById.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Public (no token required); returns 200 with { token, profile } for the seeded credentials.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Non-200 (e.g. 401) fails the stage; token must be a non-empty string and profile.id/email must match the seed.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires a valid bearer token (the login token); actor resolved from request.user, never a client-supplied id.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: 200 with the exact 10-field EmployeeProfile; passwordHash/terminationDate absent.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires a valid bearer token; EMPLOYEE role scoping to the owner's own requests.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: 200 with an array containing the seeded request id.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires a valid bearer token; EMPLOYEE may read only their own request.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: 200 returning the seeded request (id and employeeId match).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires a valid bearer token; actor resolved from request.user.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: 200 with EXACTLY one balance (ANNUAL); SICK omitted; available === 25.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The current-period re-key must use periodContaining imported from src/shared/date (the same helper getCurrentBalances uses), never a hand-written date, so the assertion matches the service for whatever new Date() is at run time.
The seeded employee's password_hash must be minted with the SAME bcrypt call the app verifies against (hashSync(plaintext, 10)) so the login stage's bcrypt.compare succeeds.
The stage 5 profile assertion must match the exact 10-field EmployeeProfile shape (no passwordHash, no terminationDate) returned by getEmployeeProfileById.

The stage 8 balance assertion must match getCurrentBalances' output contract: available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays, and an effective policy with no balance row is omitted (never synthesized).
The stage 6/7 list/getById assertions must match the EMPLOYEE role scoping in LeaveService.list/getById (owner sees only their own requests).
The login token must be verified by the same registerAuth preHandler that populates request.user from payload.sub/role, so stages 5–8 exercise real auth end to end.

integrationPoints.why: Re-key the seeded balance to the current accrual period using the same helper getCurrentBalances uses, so the assertion is date-independent.
Stages 3b/3c mint a hand token; stages 5–8 must use the genuine login token verified by registerAuth.
Seed rows and assertions reference the canonical enums so values match the app's persisted/returned values.
Seed and re-key queries run against the per-run SCHEMA search_path so they hit the same schema the app serves.
